test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, the Government of India announced which of the following missions for ensuring energy reliability and reducing dependency on fossil fuels?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nuclear Energy Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the presentation of the **Union Budget 2025-26**, Union Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** announced the **Nuclear Energy Mission** as a core component of India's strategy for **energy security** and **transition**.
 
• The mission focuses on the development of **Bharat Small Reactors (BSR)**, which are designed to provide decentralized and reliable power, particularly for hard-to-abate industries.
 
• A significant highlight of this mission is the promotion of **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)**, allowing the private sector to collaborate with the government in **research and development** and the deployment of nuclear technologies.
 
• The government aims to leverage **Nuclear Energy** to reduce the carbon footprint of the industrial sector, supporting the national goal of achieving **Net Zero emissions by 2070**.
 
• This initiative is part of a broader **Energy Transition Roadmap** that seeks to balance the intermittency of renewable sources like solar and wind with stable **baseload power** from nuclear sources. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nuclear Energy Mission.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Small Modular Reactors (SMRs):**
 
 
• **SMRs** are advanced nuclear reactors that have a power capacity of up to **300 MW** per unit, which is about one-third of the generating capacity of traditional nuclear power reactors.
 
• Due to their **small size**, they can be factory-constructed and transported to a site for installation, making them more affordable and flexible in terms of **location** compared to large-scale plants.
 
 
 
• **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana:**
 
 
• Announced previously and reinforced in recent fiscal discussions, this scheme aims to provide **300 units of free electricity** every month to **1 crore households** through **rooftop solar** installations.
 
• It represents a massive push toward **Renewable Energy** at the consumer level, reducing the burden on the national grid and promoting self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Mission (National Green Hydrogen Mission):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2023** with an outlay of **Rs. 19,744 crore**, this mission aims to make India a global hub for the production and export of **Green Hydrogen**.
 
• The target is to reach a production capacity of **5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)** per annum by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Net Zero Target 2070:**
 
 
• India committed to this target at the **COP26** summit in **Glasgow**. The transition involves shifting the **energy mix** from fossil fuels (coal, oil) to non-fossil sources (solar, wind, nuclear, and hydro).
 
• As of **2024-25**, India has one of the world's fastest-growing renewable energy capacities, ranking **4th** globally in total installed renewable energy capacity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL):** A **Public Sector Enterprise** under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**, it is the primary body responsible for the design, construction, and operation of nuclear power plants in India.
 
• **Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme:** Formulated by **Homi J. Bhabha**, this program aims to utilize India's vast **Thorium** reserves. The current phase primarily involves **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)**.
 
• **Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act (2010):** This act provides a framework for compensation in the event of a nuclear accident, which has been a key point of discussion regarding **Private Sector** entry into the nuclear domain.
 
• **Energy Reliability:** Unlike solar and wind, which are **intermittent**, nuclear energy provides a continuous supply of electricity, making it essential for maintaining **grid stability** as India industrializes further.
